forum.title: about Sidekick - and its level of knowledge
forum.best_answer_content:
btw     speed...  for "CLS" , fill TFT 76800 pixel in 16b color (2 byte writes) at 32Mbit : 38.4 ms theor. possible .

(core at 200MHz, optimizer -O2 , all caches ON , 64MHz for SPI4.)

With standard HAL used for pin switching and SPI i got : 204 ms ;

Now (with Gemini's tips for direct SPI programming ) i get : 38 ms (+/- 1ms , time from systick).

Close enough... I think.

scraped_replies.html:
I didnt make a test...i just tried to get "help" with this strange complicated SPI , because no useful examples also.

Just see, what the Gemini /google answered, after i wrote: its working now:

It’s great that everything is running smoothly now! For displays like the ST7789, the combination of precisely waiting for the TXC flag and manually controlling the D/C and CS GPIOs is indeed the most stable solution. Since the software overhead involved in toggling the GPIOs briefly delays execution, the display controller receives exactly the minimal pause it requires for processing. However, if you later wish to transfer large amounts of data—such as entire images or framebuffers—to the display, waiting byte-by-byte within the loop will consume a significant amount of CPU time. If you decide to optimize this project in the future, we could tackle the following steps next: Block Transfers—sending large pixel arrays in a fast "Continuous Mode" (without pauses between bytes); and DMA Support—transferring the entire image buffer to the display in the background, thereby allowing your CPU to handle other tasks simultaneously. Would you like to optimize the transmission of image data (Burst Mode) next, or is the display already running fast enough for your current application?

--- too much for tonight, but ... can you feel some difference in level ?
